items.title: Uniformly computable arrays of thin colourings whose thin sets compute the k-th Turing jump
items.author: Lorenzo Carlucci; Oriola Gjetaj; Quentin Le Houérou; Ludovic Levy Patey
items.work: Ramsey-like theorems for the Schreier barrier
items.difficulty_reason: The counted unit is Lemma lem:arrays at source lines 683-685: two arrays of Turing indexes must be produced so that the k-th-jump-computable colourings f_n^k from n-element subsets onto n colours exist uniformly in n and k and every infinite f_n^k-thin set computes the k-th jump through the single index d_{n,k}. The colouring at source line 690 encodes a uniform modulus g_k of the k-th jump into a colour by comparing x_1 with g_k(x_0) and otherwise returning the largest i < n-1 with g_k(x_0) > x_{i+1}, and the three steps that follow are each needed: the top colour n-1 is avoided outright (line 692), thinness for any smaller colour c has to be pushed up to the colour n-2 by extending a tuple beyond g_k(x_0) (line 694), and only then does thinness for n-2 give the growth bound g_k(x_i) <= x_{i+n-1} which makes the jump computable from H (line 696). The uniformity in n and k, which the finite-dimensional result this lemma improves does not supply, is what cannot be obtained by quoting that result, and the article says so in the paragraph preceding the lemma.
